description:
GZL Energy Biogas Plant is a biogas-to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from cattle manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented by GZL ENERJİ ANONİM ŞİRKETİ in Çınarlık village, Çarşamba district, Samsun province, in Turkey. 

Çarşamba is the third-largest district in Samsun province in terms of the number of animals registered. However, whilst number of animal farms has substantially increased for the last years in the region, cattle manure generated at farms, which is left to decay at and around farms in aerobic conditions, has become a major environmental, economic and legal problem for cattle breeders and poultry farmers, as well as for the local people living around farms. The project whose main feedstock will be cattle and chicken manure generated at farms in Çarşamba, provides an environmentally friendly solution to this manure management problem.

Within the scope of the project, biodegradation of organic wastes coming to the Biogas Plant in anaerobic environment will take place. The biogas that will be released during the biodegradation of organic wastes will be used for electricity and heat production in biogas unit. The proposed project activity has one biogas engine installed at the biogas power plant, with a total capacity of 1,501 KWe/h. The project is expected to generate 12,968,640 kWh of renewable energy annually.

The proposed project activity is expected to generate 52,346 tCO2eq emission reductions per annum through 
•	preventing GHG emissions, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from cattle manure that would be otherwise left to decay in aerobic conditions;
•	replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the Turkish grid which is heavily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources by generating renewable energy and feeding it to the grid.
